conviction_note: The quarter itself very likely beats a bar set at management's own conservative guide: tech is 58% of revenue, backlog entered Q3 +69% same-store, and Census data-center construction spending accelerated through Q3 (+65% YoY in July, +73% in August). But FIX sold its last two beats (-5.3%, -2.7%), and on the day of the print the AI-infrastructure tape is selling beats (Lam -10% on a beat, Meta down). The stock has already de-rated about 30% since Oct 6, including -8.4% intraday today, so the bar is lower. I lean slightly up (p_up 55) on an 11-point absolute move, which gives +1.1. The findings sum to +0.8 and the two numbers agree.

findings.finding: The quarter's revenue is likely to clear the $3.39B (+38% YoY) bar by a few percent. Backlog entered Q3 at $14.06B (+73% YoY; same-store +69%, $13.70B). Technology/data-center work was 58% of H1 revenue. Q2 revenue already grew +50% YoY ($3.27B) and beat consensus $2.99B by 9%, with EPS of $12.53 against $10.45. The independent Census series shows private data-center construction spending accelerating through the quarter: +55% YoY in June, +65% in July, and +73% in August to a record $84.95B SAAR. My read is revenue about $3.50-3.55B (+3-5% vs bar) and EPS above $13.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large beats have been sold lately. Q2 2026: revenue +9% and EPS +20% vs consensus, and the stock fell 5.33%. Q1 2026: big beat, -2.69%. Q4 2025: 39% EPS beat, +6.46%. Q3 2025: +18.99%. Q2 2025: +22.37%. The payoff to a beat has shrunk to negative over the last two prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at +38% YoY sits on management's conservative 'mid to high 30%' guide rather than on the +50% run-rate and the accelerating Q3 spending series. If the market had priced a ~5% revenue beat, the estimate would have been revised up further than +0.34% in 60 days, and the stock would not be at -30% from its Oct 6 close into the print. The direction of the beat is broadly expected (four straight large beats), so this is sized small.

findings.finding: Management has raised its FY2026 same-store revenue-growth guide every quarter: 'mid-teens to high-teens' (2026-02-19), then 'mid- to high-20%' (2026-04-23), then 'mid to high 30%' (2026-07-23). H1 grew about 53% ($6.13B vs $4.00B). The current guide implies only about 25% H2 growth on FY2025 revenue of $9.10B. A fourth raise, to about 40%+, is the likely guidance content of this release or call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 raise (+10 points, to mid-high 30s) came with a -5.33% reaction. The Q1 raise (+10 points, to mid-high 20s) came with -2.69%. Raises have not been paid for in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: street Q3 (+38%) and FY EPS ($48.15) already run above the company's guided path, so a raise mostly catches the guide up to the street. What would be unpriced is a raise well above the street (e.g. 'mid-40s'), which the Q3 spending acceleration makes possible but not documented. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Prior guide steps: Q4 2025 release/call 'mid-teens to high-teens' (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260219524928/en/Comfort-Systems-USA-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results) and Q1 2026 'mid- to high-20%' (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4579638-comfort-systems-forecasts-mid-to-high-20-percent-2026-same-store-revenue-growth-as-backlog). Shares the Q2 document with finding 1 for the H1 numbers only.

findings.finding: FIX has de-rated about 30% into the print, with no company-specific news: from a 1,817.96 close on Oct 6 to about 1,284 intraday on Oct 22, including -8.4% today. The cause is sector-wide AI-financing fear: CoreWeave debt stress, hot September CPI, oil above $110, Meta's funding plans, and Nvidia's CEO calling capital scarce. Goldman cut its target to $1,875 from $2,159 on Oct 20 but kept Buy. The multiple now carries a much lower bar going into a company-level print that management will use to talk about bookings and modular sell-outs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came after a pre-print slide (-6.6% on Jul 2, -6.1% on Jul 7, and an Erste downgrade), and the stock still fell 5.33% on a beat. A pre-print drawdown has not guaranteed relief on this name. Q3 2025 (Oct 2025), after AI jitters, returned +18.99%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about the price itself, not a hidden fact. The point is that the de-rating came from sector financing fears, not from any FIX number, so a clean company-level bookings print can reprice it. If the market had already priced a strong print, the stock would not have fallen 8% on the print day alongside chipmakers. Sized small, because 'oversold into a print' is not a mechanism by itself.

Meta fell 5-7% after a revenue beat while narrowing 2026 capex up. The chip index was down about 6%. FIX's own last two beats were also sold. A beat-and-raise may not be enough in this tape unless backlog growth is large.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat and raise: -5.33%. Q1 2026 beat and raise: -2.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since the stock is already down 8% today. What is not priced is the reaction function: a straddle at 11.5% says 'large move', and skew at +0.55 says no direction. If the market expected a relief rally, the call side would be bid against puts.

findings.finding: Forward data-center planning is cooling while current spending is at a record. The Dodge Momentum Index for September 2026 shows commercial planning -1.3% m/m, driven by data center and warehouse cooling, and -14.9% YoY excluding data centers. Oracle/OpenAI dropped the Abilene Stargate expansion (1.2 to 2.0 GW). 30-50% of 16 GW of 2026 US capacity is reportedly delayed (a figure SemiAnalysis disputes). The risk is that Q3 bookings, and so backlog growth (Q2 added $1.61B), come in light. Backlog is the line the stock has traded on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog has risen every quarter: $9.38B (Q3'25), $11.94B (Q4'25), $12.45B (Q1'26), $14.06B (Q2'26). The small Q1 2026 backlog step (+$0.51B) came with a -2.69% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced through the 30% de-rating and Goldman's 'capex durability' target cut. Dodge planning leads construction by about a year, and FIX management said its modular capacity is 'farther and farther booked out'. This is a proxy, not a company number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Stacker/KVIA 2026-10-20 on delays and cancellations: https://kvia.com/stacker-technology/2026/10/20/tech-companies-need-more-data-centers-so-why-are-nearly-half-of-all-planned-projects-delayed-or-canceled/. Against it, the broader Census current-spending series (+73% YoY, Aug) points the other way for the reported quarter.

findings.finding: Meta, a hyperscaler data-center builder, reported Q3 on 2026-10-21. It narrowed 2026 capex up to $135-145B, from $130-145B, after FIX last spoke. That is a direct customer-class signal that 2026 building is not being cut, even though the market read it as a financing worry.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No FIX-specific history on hyperscaler capex updates in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The market sold Meta and AI infrastructure on the financing angle. The demand read for contractors (capex range raised at the low end) is not reflected in FIX's -8% today. FIX's customers are not named, so this transmission is a proxy.

findings.finding: FIX held $1.85B cash and $54M debt at 2026-06-30, plus roughly $1B of Q2 free cash flow. It returned only $61M YTD (dividends) against $284.8M in 2025, and the stock is 38% off its high. That leaves room for a buyback step-up or new authorization announced with the print. The company's 2007-2025 deployment was 18% repurchases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history on buyback announcements.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only. No authorization change is documented and management prefers acquisitions (71% of deployment). If it were expected, it would appear in previews, and none mention it.

Rule 6 (inside what is guided): the guidance-raise finding was trimmed +0.8 -> +0.5, because street numbers already sit above the company's guided path.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not a cause): drawdown/relief positioning trimmed +1.5 -> +0.8. The drawdown has a sector cause, but 'oversold into a print' is not a mechanism by itself.

Rule 3 (read the set): the tape-sells-beats finding was trimmed -1.5 -> -1.2 so the two positioning findings do not double-count one tape.
